value_stream.name: Corporate Development, Mergers & Acquisitions, Divestiture & Strategic Transactions

fields.Owner: Integration Lead / Head of Corporate Development
fields.Participants: Integration Lead, Corp Dev, all workstreams, COO, CFO, affected business unit, PMO (links to VS-112), Strategy (links to VS-33)

workflows.name: Post-Merger Integration (PMI) Strategy, Planning & Synergy Realization

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "Integration Lead define the PMI strategy and guiding principles" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "Integration Lead build the integration plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report progress to the steering committee and Board" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: bottom-up tracking and accountability; operational: intensity-tailored approach
Pain Points / Risks: - **Synergy-shortfall risk**: Targeted synergies not realized; mitigated by bottom-up tracking and accountability
- **Integration-overreach risk**: Over-integration destroying acquired value; mitigated by intensity-tailored approach
System Touchpoints: - PMO (links to VS-112); strategy (links to VS-33); finance (links to VS-17.4); governance (links to VS-36); analytics (links to VS-28)

steps.activity: Integration Lead define the PMI strategy and guiding principles: value-creation thesis, integration intensity (full absorption vs preservation), integration operating model and governance, synergy targets (revenue/cost/financial), and the integration roadmap with value-capture milestones

Integration Lead build the integration plan: workstream plans (commercial, operations, finance, HR, IT, legal), synergy-tracking (baseline, target, owner, date), dependencies, risks, and budget — leveraging PMO discipline (links to VS-112) and the Day-1 plan (links to W3994)
Integration Lead execute synergy realization, track value capture against baseline, manage integration risks, and report progress to the steering committee and Board (links to VS-36)

fields.Participants: Integration Lead, Legal (links to VS-100), Finance/Treasury, HR, IT, Tax (links to VS-79), Corp Sec (links to VS-36.1), affected business unit, communications (links to VS-14.3)

workflows.name: Day-1 Readiness, Cutover & Transaction Close Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accounts and treasury" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "Legal/Integration-Lead manage closing" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: Day-1 plan and runbook; operational: tracking and early resolution
Pain Points / Risks: - **Day-1-disruption risk**: Operations/payroll/IT disrupted at close; mitigated by Day-1 plan and runbook
- **Conditions-failure risk**: Closing blocked by unsatisfied conditions; mitigated by tracking and early resolution
System Touchpoints: - Legal/corp sec (links to VS-100/VS-36.1); finance/treasury (links to VS-17/VS-18); HR/payroll (links to VS-19); consolidation (links to VS-72); comms (links to VS-14.3)

steps.activity: Integration Lead prepare Day-1 readiness: legal-entity and signatory setup, bank accounts and treasury (links to VS-18), payroll/HR continuity (links to VS-19), customer/vendor continuity, financial close and consolidation (links to VS-72/VS-17), and Day-1 communications (internal links to VS-103.1; external links to VS-14.3)
Legal/Integration-Lead manage closing: conditions-satisfaction (links to W3992), funds flow, signing/closing mechanics, share/asset transfer, and post-close actions checklist
Integration Lead execute Day-1 cutover, stabilize operations, and transition to full integration (links to W3993/W3995/W3996)

fields.Participants: IT (links to VS-27/VS-113), Enterprise Architecture (links to VS-113), Master Data (links to VS-29), Data/Analytics (links to VS-28), ITAM (links to VS-99), affected business unit

workflows.name: Systems, Data & ERP Integration for Acquired Entities

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "IT/EA plan systems integration onto BuildRight's unified cloud ERP" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-test of "testing, and cutover with rollback — minimizing disruption to live trading" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validate post-cutover, and transition to BAU support" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: cleansing, testing, and rollback; operational: EA-led integration
Pain Points / Risks: - **Migration risk**: Data loss/corruption during cutover; mitigated by cleansing, testing, and rollback
- **Architecture-drift risk**: Acquired systems creating landscape incoherence; mitigated by EA-led integration
System Touchpoints: - IT/EA (links to VS-27/VS-113); MDM (links to VS-29); analytics (links to VS-28); ITAM (links to VS-99); privacy (links to VS-91)

steps.activity: IT/EA plan systems integration onto BuildRight's unified cloud ERP and enterprise architecture (links to VS-113): migration vs retirement vs coexistence, integration sequence, master-data harmonization (items, customers, vendors, locations, COA links to VS-29), and security/identity integration (links to VS-27)

IT execute the migration/cutover: data cleansing and migration, ERP configuration, integrations (POS/ecommerce/payments/suppliers), testing, and cutover with rollback — minimizing disruption to live trading
IT decommission legacy systems securely (links to VS-99 ITAM/secure retirement and VS-91 data privacy), validate post-cutover, and transition to BAU support (links to VS-27)

fields.Participants: HR (links to VS-19/VS-102/VS-103), Communications (links to VS-14.3/VS-103.1), affected leaders/managers, Legal, Change Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "tracking, and remediation of attrition/culture risks" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: retention and engagement; operational: culture assessment and integration
Pain Points / Risks: - **Talent-flight risk**: Acquired talent leaving during/after integration; mitigated by retention and engagement
- **Culture-clash risk**: Cultural mismatch undermining value; mitigated by culture assessment and integration
System Touchpoints: - HR (links to VS-19/VS-102/VS-103); comms (links to VS-14.3/VS-103.1); labor relations (links to VS-84); ethics (links to VS-119); L&D (links to VS-19.4/VS-123)

steps.activity: HR design the integrated organization: org structure, role mapping and selection process, leadership team, compensation harmonization (links to VS-102), retention of key talent, and any restructuring/retrenchment under DOLE (links to VS-84/VS-19.5)

HR/Communications manage culture and change: vision and narrative, culture assessment and integration plan, communications cadence (links to VS-103.1), engagement and listening, and adoption of BuildRight's standards/code of conduct (links to VS-119)
HR sustain the integration: training and onboarding to BuildRight (links to VS-19.4/VS-123/VS-124), engagement tracking, and remediation of attrition/culture risks

workflows.name: Carve-Out, Separation & Transitional Service Agreement (TSA) Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "track TSA exit/migration" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validate standalone operation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: exit tracking; operational: clear pricing and exit discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stand-up-delay risk**: Standalone capability not ready when TSA ends; mitigated by exit tracking
- **TSA-cost-overrun risk**: TSA charges escalating; mitigated by clear pricing and exit discipline
System Touchpoints: - Legal (links to VS-100); finance/intercompany (links to VS-72/VS-17.4); IT (links to VS-27/VS-113); HR (links to VS-19); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Corp Dev/Integration-Lead scope the carve-out/separation: separating shared systems/data/processes, stand-up of standalone capabilities, transition planning, and the TSA framework (services, pricing, duration, exit) — when acquiring a carve-out or divesting a portion

Corp Dev/Legal negotiate and execute TSAs (providing/receiving services with seller/buyer), manage TSA service delivery and charges (links to VS-72 intercompany where relevant), and track TSA exit/migration
Integration Lead execute stand-up and TSA exit on plan, minimize dependence, and validate standalone operation

fields.Trigger: Portfolio decision to divest (links to W3977); non-strategic asset/category/entity

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepare the disposal business case, and recommend to the approval authority" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "accounting and tax" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: competitive process and valuation; operational: clean separation and TSA
Pain Points / Risks: - **Value-leakage risk**: Disposing below fair value; mitigated by competitive process and valuation
- **Separation risk**: Carve-out disrupting retained operations; mitigated by clean separation and TSA
System Touchpoints: - Finance/assets (links to VS-17.4/VS-35/VS-40); tax (links to VS-79); legal (links to VS-100); strategy (links to VS-33); competition (links to VS-129)

steps.activity: Corp Dev/Strategy identify and scope divestiture candidates (stores, categories, entities, non-core assets) against portfolio strategy (links to W3977), prepare the disposal business case, and recommend to the approval authority (links to W3983)

Corp Dev/external-advisors run the sale process: vendor DD, marketing, buyer approach, valuation, SPA negotiation (links to W3991), carve-out/separation (links to W3997), and regulatory clearance (links to W3992)
Finance/Tax/Legal execute disposal accounting and tax (gain/loss, links to VS-35/VS-40/VS-17.4/VS-79), manage separation and TSA (links to W3997), and capture value realized (links to W4000)

workflows.name: Joint Venture & Strategic Partnership Post-Close Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-post of "Corp Dev/Legal establish the JV/partnership post-close" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "JV GM/Corp-Dev manage the JV in-life" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "review, exit/dispute resolution, buy-sell/drag/tag rights, and…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: clear governance and rights; operational: dispute-resolution and deadlock-break mechanisms
Pain Points / Risks: - **Partner-misalignment risk**: Partners diverging on strategy/operations; mitigated by clear governance and rights
- **Deadlock risk**: Decisions blocked; mitigated by dispute-resolution and deadlock-break mechanisms
System Touchpoints: - Legal/contracts (links to VS-100/VS-36); consolidation/intercompany (links to VS-72/VS-17.4); competition (links to VS-129); finance (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Corp Dev/Legal establish the JV/partnership post-close: governance (board/committee, partner rights), operating model, business plan, capitalization and funding, and the shareholders'/JV agreement terms (links to VS-100/VS-36)

JV GM/Corp-Dev manage the JV in-life: performance against plan, partner relationship, decisions requiring consent, contributions/distributions, accounting/consolidation treatment (links to VS-72/VS-17.4), and competition compliance (links to VS-129 W3963)
Corp Dev manage JV/partnership lifecycle: performance review, exit/dispute resolution, buy-sell/drag/tag rights, and renewal/termination (links to VS-100/VS-36)

workflows.name: M&A Portfolio Performance, Value Realization & Lessons-Learned Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Corp Dev/Finance track each transaction's value realization" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Corp Dev run post-deal reviews" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-create of "created vs invested, hit-rate, integration health, and forward pipeline" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-622 (ensure controlled execution — Integration, Carve-Out, Divestiture & Post-Merger Performance (PA-130.3).)
- operational: tracking vs deal model; operational: post-deal reviews and feedback loops
Pain Points / Risks: - **Value-blindness risk**: BuildRight cannot tell if deals created value; mitigated by tracking vs deal model
- **Lesson-loss risk**: Lessons not captured/reapplied; mitigated by post-deal reviews and feedback loops
System Touchpoints: - Finance (links to VS-17.4); analytics (links to VS-28); strategy (links to VS-33); governance (links to VS-36); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Corp Dev/Finance track each transaction's value realization: synergy capture vs plan, financial performance vs deal model, integration milestones, and value-killer/lesson log

Corp Dev run post-deal reviews (90-day, 1-year, anniversaries), capture lessons learned (DD gaps, integration effectiveness, valuation accuracy), and feed back into the strategy/framework (links to W3977/W3978)

Corp Dev report the M&A portfolio to the Board (links to VS-36): aggregate value created vs invested, hit-rate, integration health, and forward pipeline (links to W3979), and adjust the corporate-development strategy/budget
